description: Amounts read from JSON (receipts, ledger rows). imd-flop: knownAmount(v) and usableCapCharge(v). spend-guard: spend_amount(v) and json_number(v). viewer: amount(v). {"$float": "nan"|"inf"|"-inf"} encodes non-finite floats.

vectors.note: Review fixes 2 (R10): above AMOUNT_MAX (then 2^53 - 1, the largest integer a double holds exactly; 1e9 FLOP since swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 5) an amount is unknown in imd-flop and the viewer. Before, 1e308 was a known amount. spend-guard is outside R10 and keeps its own rule.
swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 5: AMOUNT_MAX itself, 1e9 FLOP, is a known amount in both parts
finding 5: one 1e-6 step above AMOUNT_MAX is not a known amount in either part
2^53 - 1. It was AMOUNT_MAX (review fixes 2, R10). Since swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 5, AMOUNT_MAX is 1e9 FLOP, so it is above it and unknown in both parts. spend-guard has no such bound.
Review fixes 2 (R10): 2^53 is above AMOUNT_MAX, so it is unknown in both parts, never a guess.

Review fixes 2 (R10): 2^53 + 1. Python reads this JSON integer exactly; JavaScript's JSON.parse reads it as 2^53. Both are above AMOUNT_MAX, so both parts call it unknown and give the same verdict on the same text.
